title: 〜に比べて / 〜に比べ
simpleExplanation: 〜に比べて sets up a comparison: "Compared with X, Y is …". X is the reference point; the main clause states how Y differs (more, less, higher, quieter). It is neutral, does not imply that either side is better, and works for any noun: times, places, people, products.
whenUsed: Both speech and writing. に比べると and に比べたら are conversational variants; に比べ (without て) is written or formal spoken style found in news and reports. Very common with statistics and trends.
formation: Noun + に比べて / に比べ / に比べると / に比べたら
Clause + の + に比べて (以前働いていたのに比べて)
Main clause: comparative adjective or amount (多い / 高い / 少ない / 〜倍)

diagram.translation: Compared to last year, there is a lot of rain this year.

examples.ja: 去年に比べて、今年は雨が多い。
examples.reading: きょねんにくらべて、ことしはあめがおおい。
examples.en: Compared to last year, there is a lot of rain this year.
examples.note: Comparing two times; the main clause gives the difference (雨が多い).

examples.ja: 都会に比べ、田舎は物価が安い。
examples.reading: とかいにくらべ、いなかはぶっかがやすい。
examples.en: Compared to the city, prices in the countryside are low.
examples.note: に比べ without て: written, formal style.

examples.ja: 兄に比べると、弟はおとなしい。
examples.reading: あににくらべると、おとうとはおとなしい。
examples.en: Compared with his older brother, the younger one is quiet.
examples.note: に比べると: conversational variant; comparison of two people.

examples.ja: 昔に比べて、女性の社会進出が進んだ。
examples.reading: むかしにくらべて、じょせいのしゃかいしんしゅつがすすんだ。
examples.en: Compared with the past, women's participation in society has advanced.
examples.note: Typical essay use with a social trend.

examples.ja: 一人で勉強するのに比べたら、先生に教わるほうがずっと効率的だ。
examples.reading: ひとりでべんきょうするのにくらべたら、せんせいにおそわるほうがずっとこうりつてきだ。
examples.en: Compared with studying alone, being taught by a teacher is far more efficient.
examples.note: Clause + のに比べたら: casual, with ほうが in the main clause.

similarGrammar.difference: The basic comparison particle; shorter and more casual. に比べて frames the comparison more explicitly and is favored in explanations and statistics.
Marks a contrast between two different things ("whereas"), not a degree comparison. 兄は活発なのに対して、弟は静かだ.
"Considering": the result is out of proportion to the standard, not a neutral comparison.
"For a…": the result deviates from what the category leads you to expect.

commonMistakes.wrong: 東京に比べて、大阪は物価が安いです。→ 大阪に比べて東京は物価が安いです。 (reversed)
commonMistakes.right: 東京に比べて、大阪は物価が安い。
commonMistakes.why: The noun before に比べて is the reference; the subject after it is the one being described. Reversing them reverses the meaning.

commonMistakes.wrong: 去年に比べて、今年は雨だ。
commonMistakes.right: 去年に比べて、今年は雨が多い。
commonMistakes.why: The main clause must express a difference in degree or amount, not just a plain fact.

commonMistakes.wrong: 兄に比べて、弟は静かだのに。
commonMistakes.right: 兄に比べて、弟は静かだ。
commonMistakes.why: Do not mix in contrast markers like のに; に比べて already frames the comparison.

usageNotes: に比べ (no て) belongs to written style: 前年に比べ、三割増加した.
Numbers are common after it: 〜に比べて二倍 / 三割 / 一〇ポイント高い.
For a whole clause, insert の: 一人で行くのに比べて.
jlptTips: If the main clause contains a comparative amount (多い, 少ない, 高い, 倍), に比べて is likely. If it contrasts two different qualities (whereas), choose に対して.
Check the connection: a verb clause needs の before に比べて.
In 並べ替え, に比べて normally sits right after the reference noun and before the subject + は.
